gaps.category: Monotributo / autónomos / simplified-regime recategorization and household-level ARCA duties for sole traders (not generic accounting)
gaps.first_search: recategorización monotributo ARCA 2026 régimen simplificado cambios RG exclusión parámetros
gaps.why: Millions of monotributistas must recategorize semiannually (Jan/Jul) and face exclusion checks; a different buyer group from K11 and not covered in the 36 categories. Unsure whether free ARCA simulators kill it, but not checked.

gaps.category: Taxi, remís, app-driver and school-transport licensing (provincial/municipal) plus RTO/VTV and driver ficha
gaps.first_search: renovación habilitación remís taxi municipalidad requisitos VTV obligatoria 2026 ordenanza
gaps.why: Cat. 18 only found fragmented school transport. Taxis/remises have mandatory periodic municipal habilitation, VTV, libreta sanitaria and insurance, and a large owner base. Also VTV/RTO workshops as small operators were not probed.

gaps.category: Cannabis/hemp and other new regulated agri-lines: industrial hemp (cáñamo) producers under ARICCAME/Decreto 405/2023 and seed producers (INASE registers)
gaps.first_search: INASE inscripción registro comercial semillas declaración jurada anual multiplicadores 2026 resolución
gaps.why: Cat. 33 covers REPROCANN only. INASE seed multipliers, RNCyFS registers and hemp growers have annual declarations; many small farms. Not in coverage table.

gaps.category: Small mining, lapidary, fishing and artisanal fisheries: Registro de Pesca / SENASA fish plants and CFP permits
gaps.first_search: declaración jurada de captura pesca artesanal permiso de pesca Subsecretaría de Pesca resolución 2026 desembarques obligatoria
gaps.why: Argentina has many small fishing boat owners and processing plants with mandatory catch declarations and landings reports; Mar del Plata/Chubut clusters. Category 30 mentions fish only as exports; no catch-reporting duty searched.

gaps.category: Municipal tasas, habilitación comercial renewals and Ingresos Brutos local regimes (ARBA/AGIP/Rentas, Convenio Multilateral SIFERE/SIRCREB, padrón de agentes de retención)
gaps.first_search: Convenio Multilateral CM05 anual 2026 cambios SIFERE pequeños contribuyentes régimen simplificado ingresos brutos
gaps.why: Provincial gross-income duties (monthly DDJJ, agentes de percepción/retención, CM03/CM05 Convenio Multilateral) fall on every small firm and sole trader; none of the 36 categories touches ingresos brutos or habilitaciones comerciales municipal renewal. Likely competitive, but must be screened.

gaps.category: Consorcios de propietarios (property-administrator duties: RPA registry, expensas, labour of encargados/porteros, SUTERH F.931)

gaps.why: Consorcios are the largest household-style employer group (building doormen/encargados) and administrators must be registered (CABA RPA Ley 941, annual renewal; provincial equivalents). Only the elevator angle was touched; K16 covers domestic staff only.

candidates.buyer: Licensed desarmaderos and used-autoparts sellers (small family yards), plus the businesses that handle parts
candidates.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
candidates.existing: Competitor search 'software gestión desarmadero autopartes RUDAC' found no commercial product, only the rules (not conclusive). Generic autoparts ERP/stock tools not checked. DNRPA platform is the state channel.
candidates.known_note: Different buyer (car dismantlers, not scrap and non-ferrous dealers) and different duty (RUDAC part traceability, not provincial scrap books). Related to K06.
candidates.name: RUDAC digital dismantler operations book: vehicle-to-part traceability, part codes, photos and stock declaration
candidates.trigger: Ley 25.761; Decreto 536/2025 (removed annual renewal, mandatory online baja and part declaration with photos, DNRPA part identification code); DNRPA Disp. 730/2025 (new TAD-based RUDAC regime) and 732/2025 (identifier model); Disp. 545/2025 (baja with part recovery); Disp. 123/2026 reportedly replaced the identifier. Police inspect stock. Records kept 10 years.
candidates.unchecked: Exact current identifier (Disp. 123/2026) and whether DNRPA offers an API or bulk upload; number of registered desarmaderos; any unconfirmed registration deadline; whether DNRPA platform already handles most workflow for free; existing autoparts stock systems (e.g. ERP for repuestos) adding RUDAC modules.

candidates.buyer: Small faenadores: municipal and provincial abattoirs, matarifes and abastecedores with own slaughter; related carnicerías for REC
candidates.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
candidates.existing: State SIF/SIGICA portal; no private SIF bridge product found. Competitor search for this not run (budget). REC tooling unchecked.
candidates.known_note: K03 is the producer/feedlot RFID reconciliation for the SENASA movement record; this is the slaughter-side buyer (faenadores) and duty (SIF records). Related to K03.
candidates.name: SIF electronic slaughter records for small, municipal and provincial slaughterhouses and matarifes (stock, romaneo, REC, e-ID at line)
candidates.trigger: Min. Economía Res. 40/2026 (SIF, in force 1 Jan 2026; data is declaración jurada; physical stock and egress books replaced by digital 'Existencias de Carne'; REC mandatory); Res. 50/2026 requires reading electronic ID on the slaughter line from 1 Jul 2026 (already past). SENASA plants use SIGICA, treated as equivalent. National level, enforced by DNCCA.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the SIF web portal already offers batch upload or an API; number of small faenadores in scope; whether small municipal plants are in scope at the same dates; text of Res. 40/2026 and 50/2026 in Boletín Oficial (edition 337796, 27 Jan 2026); competitor search; RFID reader hardware vendors bundling this.

candidates.buyer: Small desagote and atmospheric-truck operators in Mendoza; generators that hire them (also similar municipal registers in Santa Fe/Rosario and OSSE manifest in Buenos Aires province)
candidates.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
candidates.existing: No software found. Competitor search not run (budget).

candidates.name: Mendoza Ley 9.706 atmospheric-truck register, manifest and canon for effluent haulers
candidates.trigger: Mendoza Ley 9.706 (2026, provincial) creates the public Registro Provincial de Transportistas run by Dpto. General de Irrigación; no operation without valid registration; canon; press reports a load manifest with declaración jurada value and geolocation (one source did not mention manifest, so unverified). Santa Fe Res. 145/2007 requires municipal registers; OSSE requires a manifest at its plants.
candidates.unchecked: Law publication date, reglamentación and registration deadline; whether the manifest is electronic and run by Irrigación; number of operators (likely hundreds in Mendoza only); other provinces copying; competitor search; municipal fragmentation.

candidates.buyer: Small livestock producers (and rural advisers who serve them) with RENSPA entry older than one year
candidates.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
candidates.existing: Competitor search found no gestoría or software service; SENASA procedure is free and self-service. Timing is tight.
candidates.known_note: K05 is the agrovet/rural vet SIGTRAZAVET bridge; this is a one-off RENSPA data-update duty. Near K03/K05 buyer groups. Related to K05.
candidates.name: RENSPA mandatory re-registration (done-for-you bulk service via agroveterinarias, agronomists and cooperatives)
candidates.trigger: SENASA Res. 679/2026 (27-29 Jul 2026): all RENSPA producers with registration or last update older than 1 year must re-register within 90 calendar days or be blocked, then deregistered. Exempt: bovine and bubaline producers in FMD-vaccination zones if updated through SIGSA. Online with Clave Fiscal/ARCA or at SENASA offices. National. Deadline falls around late Oct 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Exact entry-into-force date and deadline; whether beekeepers and other producers are in scope; whether the deadline is extended; if recurring annually afterwards (would raise score).

coverage.found: UIF Res. 54/2024 and 55/2024 (replaced Res. 28/2011) put jewellers, precious-metal buyers and dealers in the AML sujetos obligados regime. Weak candidate listed; AML software competitor not checked.

coverage.found: Strong: Decreto 536/2025 and DNRPA Disp. 730/2025 and 732/2025 created a fully digital RUDAC regime (TAD, part-level identification codes, photos, stock declaration); Disp. 123/2026 reportedly replaced the identifier. See candidate.

coverage.found: K03 known. New: SENASA Res. 723/2025 (biennial vehicle habilitation, linked to DT-e from 2025). RENSPA mandatory re-registration (Res. 679/2026). RUCA for consignatarios reportedly eliminated in 2025 (ARCA text, secondary source).

coverage.found: Res. 40/2026 (SIF) in force 1 Jan 2026: electronic intake, slaughter authorisation, romaneo, daily meat stocks; physical books eliminated; REC mandatory; Res. 50/2026 requires electronic-ID reading on the slaughter line from 1 Jul 2026. Carnicerías RUCA (Res. 306/2018) status unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K07. RENAPA free; 1,209 SENASA-approved extraction rooms (Res. 1186/2023); no 2026 change found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. Context: SENASA Res. 11/2025 marco regulatorio for veterinary products; Res. 979/1993 psychotropic regime with rubricated recetario and semi-annual buyer list to Colegio (vigencia unconfirmed).

coverage.found: Only Mendoza permit/restriction material (Irrigación resolutions; Res. 1542/17 request register). No driller licence or recurring small-business reporting found. Nothing new.

coverage.found: New: Mendoza Ley 9.706 (2026) creates Registro Provincial de Transportistas for atmospheric trucks with canon and traceability; Santa Fe Res. 145/2007 and Rosario municipal register; OSSE manifest. CABA pathogenic-waste register (Ley 154, Dec. 706/05) context for K04.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: CABA Registro de Conservación de Elevadores: QR oblea expires 31 Dec each year, renewal by 31 Mar; owner or administrator registers, conservadora validates. Boilers and pressure equipment not searched.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing concrete. ERAS covers only the AySA area; in BA province ADA/OCABA control cooperatives (Dec. 878/03, Ley 13.154). No small-system reporting duty or 2026 trigger found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K01. No search spent.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Search returned mostly Spain and Peru. Only RENATRE registration of rural employers and contractors surfaced. No agency register or 2026 trigger found. Weak coverage.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: CABA only: Ley 4977 (consolidated Ley 6.588), funeral-company register, annual declaración jurada via TAD (Disp. 32/2023). Small and single-city. No digital burial-book rule found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: IGJ RG 9/2026 (published 2 Jul 2026) changed annual financial-statement filing for asociaciones civiles and fundaciones via SODA with ARCA login; older IGJ origin-of-funds and PEP declarations. Halal and kosher not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: School transport is municipal and fragmented (Orán, Santa Fe, Gualeguaychú categories); fleet apps incl. YoFacturo gestión de flota exist. Grain CPE regime changed by RG Conjunta 5821/2026. No single 2026 trigger for small fleets found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Nothing new. BCRA 2017 rules on arbolitos; municipal feria ordinances (e.g. Santa Fe Ord. 13.008, Dec 2024). No recurring register found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Tattoo, driving schools, nurseries: municipal/provincial and fragmented (CABA Ley 1897, Ley 621, Mendoza three-agency approval). New: Decreto 697/2026 (3 Aug 2026) moves food registration to SENASA with a single national register. Hunting: national cotos and operators register, 5-year validity, annual update and insurance proof.

CABA simplified IIBB regime redesigned (AGIP Res 559/2025) and merged into Monotributo payment; new CABA transparency rule Res 169/2026 requires 'ALÍCUOTA ISIB CABA xx,xx%' legend on consumer receipts (invoicing software will cover it). Retention/perception agents: ARBA RN 7/2026 thresholds ($7,800M general), Santa Fe PARP padrón (Res API 37/2025), San Luis DPIP 10/2026; large agents only. Municipal habilitaciones: Paraná Decreto 1736/2026 (digital via SIAT, QR certificate, 4-6 year validity, post-inspection for low risk), General Belgrano auto-annual renewal blocked by tasa debt, San Antonio de Gálvez annual DDJJ via SUHAM. Trend is toward fewer renewals and municipal digitisation; no cross-municipality gap product found.

coverage.category: 36. Consorcios de propietarios: administrator duties (RPA Ley 941), expensas, encargados labour (SUTERH, F.931)
coverage.found: Strongest of the six gaps. CABA Ley 941: annual matrícula update plus one sworn DDJJ per consorcio administered via TAD (miBA level 3); Disposición DGDYPC 2615/2026 (published 10-4-2026) sets 2025 DDJJs due by 30-11-2026; Disposición 1129/2026 requires alta/baja of consorcios reported within 30 days; displays of registry certificate required; sanctions 73 administrators in H1 2026 (68 orders, ARS 122.9M), down from 191 in H1 2025. Provincial Buenos Aires registry law awaiting reglamentación (Liga del Consorcista, unverified). Software exists for expensas and some payroll: CONSO (Capterra, payroll module, ARS 2,950 start), Unitify, Octavo Piso, Mis Expensas-type platforms; none seen that specifically produces the TAD per-consorcio DDJJ file. SUTERH encargado payroll scales are union-set; bill by Bongiovanni (2024) would loosen the encargado regime, status unknown. Registered administrator count not found.

result.competitor: The free, mandatory DNRPA 'sistema RUDAC' platform plus TAD does the core job: intake and part-movement registration and assigning identifiers. No API or bulk upload was found; Disp. 732/2025 only mentions DNRPA IT staff training yards. Searches found no commercial software for Argentine desarmaderos and no RUDAC module in autoparts ERPs (not exhaustive).
result.duty: Ley 25.761 and Decreto 536/2025 (annual renewal removed). DNRPA Disp. 730/2025 (BO 6/10/2025, in force) sets categories A-F. Registration is through TAD. Parts must be identified with system-assigned elements before being offered, stocked or transported (Art. 7). Vehicle intake (A/B) and part movements (D) must be recorded digitally and chronologically in the DNRPA 'sistema RUDAC' (Arts. 8-9), and the records stay available to oversight bodies (Art. 10). Existing holders had to file a one-time sworn stock declaration within 90 days (Art. 11). Data changes must be reported within 5 days, and criminal-record certificates renewed yearly. Penalties are suspension or revocation after police or judicial reports, or when an inspection is blocked (Arts. 13-15). Disp. 732/2025 sets the digital baja con recuperación de piezas and the identifier model. Disp. 123/2026 (signed 25/06/2026) replaced the identifier with a more secure element (economis summary; full annex not read). The 5-photo requirement found is in Disp. 545/2025, not 730/2025.
result.market: No official count of RUDAC registrants was found. La Nación (Oct 2025) cites CaRVA's estimate of 5-7 illegal yards for every legal one, which points to a small formal base. Category D (used-parts sellers) widens the scope, but there is no figure for it. Not reached: DNRPA statistics or a public RUDAC list.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under DNRPA Disp. 730/2025 (in force since 6 Oct 2025), RUDAC holders in category A/B must log incoming vehicles, and category D sellers must log part movements, in chronological order through the free state "sistema RUDAC" (Arts. 8-9). Parts must carry the system-assigned identifier (Art. 7), and data changes must be reported within 5 days. The core record-keeping therefore lives inside a mandatory, free state system. I found no API or bulk upload, so outside software would mean entering data twice or be generic inventory software. No commercial RUDAC product was found. Not verified: the number of registered yards (CaRVA says 5-7 illegal yards per legal one, so the legal base is small) and how Disp. 123/2026's identifier works.

result.competitor: Free state channel: UIF's SRO/SRO+ portal and the SROMasivo application handle the monthly report (RSM) filing for property sales, with a defined form (buyer and seller, PEP status, payment method). The state therefore covers the report submission step, but not the risk matrix, client file and due diligence management, the self-assessment or alert monitoring. Free templates: the FACPCE ITAER guide and matrix, and the property registry's (DNRPI) matrix. Real estate CRMs (Tokko Broker, Xintel) showed no AML or UIF module in my searches. I found no broker-specific AML SaaS, though the search was not exhaustive. The main alternatives are compliance law firms (for example stabogados) and accountants.
result.duty:
Res UIF 43/2024 is national law and in force since 18 Mar 2024; the official consolidated text is on argentina.gob.ar. It covers matriculated real estate brokers and brokerage firms run by matriculated brokers, when they handle sales or leases of at least 300 SMVM a year. Duties:
- A risk self-assessment (Informe Técnico), updated every 2 years and filed by 30 April. The first was due 30 Apr 2026, so the next is due Apr 2028.
- An external independent reviewer (REI) every 2 years, within 120 days after the self-assessment deadline, for firms with income above 875 SMVM or 50+ activities a year. The first was due 31 Aug 2026.
- An internal audit instead of the REI for legal persons below those thresholds.
- Monthly systematic reports between the 1st and 15th of each month.
- An annual report (RSA) between 2 Jan and 15 Mar.
- A compliance officer, client risk segmentation with simplified, medium or enhanced due diligence, and alert signals.
Penalties: Art. 35 refers to Chapter IV of Law 25.246; I did not check the amounts. I found no 2026 extension for brokers. The 2026 extensions I found were for accountants (REI moved to 1 Mar 2027) and lawyers (Res 90/2026). There is no simplified regime for small firms.
result.market: No official count of obligated brokers was found. CUCICBA (Buenos Aires city) had 7,084 registered agencies in 2018 (BAE Negocios). FIRA estimates more than 70,000 agencies nationwide (iProfesional, Feb 2025); this is an industry-body figure and likely includes unregistered agencies. Only matriculated brokers that actually close sales or large leases are obligated, so a plausible range is roughly 10,000 to 25,000 firms (unverified). Risk: in Feb 2025 the government proposed ending mandatory colegiación for brokers; it was not enacted as of that article. If enacted, it could change who counts as an obligated subject.
result.reason: The duty is real and current. The monthly and annual reports are ongoing, and the self-assessment and external review (REI) recur every two years. Nothing dedicated does the core work of the risk matrix, client segmentation, client file and due diligence, and alert monitoring for brokers. However, the UIF's free SROMasivo/SRO already handles the monthly report submission. The heavy deliverables, the self-assessment and REI, are biennial (next due Apr/Aug 2028) and are usually bought from accountants or lawyers. Many small brokers have few qualifying operations and enforcement looks light, so willingness to pay is uncertain. Distribution through the provincial broker colegios is feasible. An MVP covering client risk scoring, the client file and RSM export is simple. Partnering with accountants who do the REI could help.
